acceptance: A preserved/continuation worktree is re-based onto current plane main (merge or rebase of the lane branch; conflicts -> honest FAIL with a named conflict, never silent) BEFORE the build phase runs — or at minimum before atomic-ship staging — so a lane never ships against a tree missing already-landed pipeline fixes.

Regression test: a preserved worktree based at HEAD~N with a .gitignore fix landed at HEAD stages a new .evolve/evals file successfully after adoption (the live cycle-1365 shape: base d323284e predating #418/42e37af2 -> GIT_STAGE_FAILED on .evolve/evals with the carve-out absent from the worktree's ladder).

The transient-retry-ship recovery detects a DETERMINISTIC stage refusal (same refused pathspec twice) and stops retrying in place — route to continuation instead of burning the retry budget on an unwinnable add.
Wiring proof over the continuation adoption seam; go vet ./..., -race green.

fix: Treat worktree base like the binary: staleness is measured against plane HEAD and healed at a boundary (continuation adoption = the worktree's boot). Rebase/merge the preserved lane branch onto current main during adoption; a conflict is an honest continuation FAIL naming the conflicting paths (the ancestor work then salvages normally). Keep preserved worktrees for their DIFF value, not their stale base.
problem: Preserved continuation worktrees keep their original checkout base forever (worktree-normalize soft-resets TO that base), so a chain that predates a landed pipeline fix ships against a tree without it — deterministically re-failing on defects the repo already fixed, re-arming the identical-fingerprint breaker the fix was meant to disarm. Live: cycle-1365 hit GIT_STAGE_FAILED on .evolve/evals twice IN the retry loop because its base predates #418; its retries are unwinnable in place. Same disease as binary lag (boot self-heal, #411) — this is the worktree-base limb of that class.
